extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: A dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task. LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages sharing the characteristic that human subjects are able to guess their last word if they are exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.
extraction.creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández
extraction.citeAs: Paperno, D., Kruszewski, G., Lazaridou, A., Pham, Q. N., Bernardi, R., Pezzelle, S., Baroni, M., Boleda, G., & Fernández, R. (2016). The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context. arXiv preprint arXiv:1606.06031.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data comes from the Book Corpus. Passages were extracted with a context of at least 50 tokens and a target sentence. Passages were filtered using language models to remove easy cases. Remaining passages were evaluated by human subjects via CrowdFlower to ensure the target word is guessable from the whole passage but not from the target sentence alone.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The Book Corpus (Zhu et al., 2015), containing unpublished novels.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Passages were filtered out if the target word had a probability >= 0.00175 according to any of four language models (pre-trained RNN, 4-gram, RNN, feed-forward).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal and filtering out of potentially offensive material with a stop word list from the Book Corpus. Context size defined as the minimum number of complete sentences before the target sentence such that they cumulatively contain at least 50 tokens. Target word constrained to be the last word of the sentence.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human subjects on CrowdFlower guessed the target word. Step 1: Guess based on whole passage. Step 2: If correct, a second subject guessed based on whole passage. Step 3: If correct, up to 10 subjects guessed based on target sentence only. Passage added to dataset if no subject guessed the word in step 3.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A strict hit-or-miss approach was used, requiring two consecutive subjects to exactly match the missing word and ensuring no subject (out of ten) could provide it based on local context only. Alternatives like including plausible or synonymous continuations were rejected due to the challenge of determining fit and financial/practical feasibility.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 (for broad context validation) + up to 10 (for local context exclusion)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Pre-trained recurrent neural network (RNN), standard 4-gram model, RNN trained on Book Corpus, feed-forward model trained on Book Corpus
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Plan to announce a public competition based on the LAMBADA data.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Potentially offensive material was filtered out using a stop word list.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Proper nouns are hugely overrepresented (48%), while other categories are under-represented. Verbs, adjectives, and adverbs are rare. Items contain direct speech significantly more often than the input items overall (71% vs 61%).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Standard language models are bound to fail by design due to the filtering process against simple language models. The dataset focuses on broad context understanding, specifically cases where local context is insufficient.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating capabilities of computational models for text understanding, specifically broad discourse context understanding via word prediction. Training, Testing, Validation.
